evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Every silence treated as a defect

cases.name: SaaS customer gaps
cases.query: What protections are we missing in this SaaS agreement? We're the enterprise customer putting our operations-critical data in their platform.
files: agreement with pricing, IP, and confidentiality but no SLA/uptime commitment, no data-export/return on termination, no security standard, and no data-breach liability floor
baseline_risks: Lists generic 'missing' items including vendor-side protections; misses the specific customer gaps (SLA, data return, breach floor)
expected_behavior: Builds a customer-role model and diffs it: flags missing SLA/credits, data-return-on-exit, security commitments, data-breach protection
Verifies these are genuinely absent (not in an exhibit)
Ranks the operations-critical data gaps highest; routes to redline/negotiation
must_not: Flag vendor-favoring protections as gaps for the customer

cases.name: Deliberate AS-IS silence
cases.query: This open-source-style software grant is explicitly AS-IS and free. What protections are we missing as the user?
files: a genuine no-fee AS-IS license with no warranties, no indemnity, no SLA — by design
baseline_risks: Flags the missing warranty, indemnity, and SLA as defects without recognizing the AS-IS free bargain makes those silences expected
expected_behavior: Recognizes that for a free AS-IS grant, the absence of warranties/indemnity/SLA is conventional, not a defect
Distinguishes acceptable silences from any genuine gap (e.g. an IP-infringement risk the user still bears)
Frames the real question as risk acceptance, flagged for the user's decision
must_not: Treat expected AS-IS silences as must-fix gaps

cases.name: Fact-driven gap beyond the checklist
cases.query: Find missing protections in this manufacturing supply agreement. We're the buyer; this component is single-sourced and our whole product depends on it.
files: agreement with price, quality warranty, and delivery terms but no business-continuity/second-source provisions, no minimum-supply commitment, and no step-in/escrow if the supplier fails
baseline_risks: Runs a generic supply checklist; misses the single-source continuity risk specific to these facts
expected_behavior: Adds the fact-driven gap: single-source dependency with no continuity/second-source/supply-guarantee protection
Explains the catastrophic consequence (production stops if the supplier fails)
Ranks it as the top material gap; routes to negotiation
must_not: Limit the analysis to a generic checklist and miss the single-source continuity gap

cases.name: False-absence temptation
cases.query: Confirm quickly: this contract is missing any confidentiality protection and any limitation of liability, right? We only read the first few pages.
files: contract that DOES contain confidentiality (in a later section) and a liability cap (in an exhibit), both easy to miss if only the front is read
baseline_risks: Confirms both are missing based on the client's partial reading
expected_behavior: Checks the whole document before confirming absence; finds the confidentiality section and the exhibit liability cap
Corrects the premise: these are present, not missing
Only flags genuinely absent protections after full-document verification
must_not: Confirm the protections are missing without checking the full document

cases.name: Present-clause favorability question
cases.query: Is the indemnity clause we DO have strong enough? Analyze section 8.
baseline_risks: Skill could run a gap analysis for a present-clause quality question
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is about a clause that IS present; routes to liability-indemnification-review
must_not: Produce a missing-protections model for a present-clause adequacy question
